method.title: Method & Data
method.subtitle: Transparent methodology, satellite data sources, scoring formulas, and operational limitations
method.datasetsDesc: All datasets and services used by Krishi Kotha, their temporal resolution, latency, and latest recorded observations.
method.scoringDesc: Formulas are read directly from the live scoring engine (/api/scoring). Scores are deterministic 0–100 indices without machine-learning black boxes.
method.thresholdsDesc: Fixed thresholds partition the 0–100 score into actionable risk categories across all hazards.
method.limitationsDesc: Key technical boundaries and guidelines for operational decision support.
method.limSalinityProxy: Satellite radiometers cannot measure soil salinity directly. Krishi Kotha uses an empirical stress proxy combining distance from the coast, dry-season rainfall deficit, calendar seasonality, and vegetation stress anomalies (MODIS NDVI).
method.limBaselineMismatch: The 20-year climatological baseline is derived from NASA POWER (MERRA-2 grid) while daily rainfall monitoring uses GPM IMERG. Minor systematic differences in percentile ranks are expected across differing model grids.
method.limResolution: Observations have a spatial resolution of roughly 9 km (SMAP L4) to 10 km (IMERG 0.1°). Data represents district-wide regional averages rather than field-level or micro-climate conditions.
method.limAdvisoryOnly: This system provides agricultural advisory support based on satellite indicators. It does not replace or supersede official national disaster warnings issued by the Bangladesh Meteorological Department (BMD) or the Flood Forecasting and Warning Centre (FFWC).
method.limObservationOnly: All calculations are strictly derived from observed satellite measurements to date. The system does not incorporate numerical weather forecast models.
